description: Fast disk usage analyzer with console interface written in Go

summary.one_liner: Gdu is a fast, parallel disk usage analyzer for the terminal written in Go, with an interactive console UI, non-interactive output modes, and an optional browser-based web UI.
summary.what_it_does: Scans one or more directories in parallel and shows which folders and files take up space, in an interactive console interface or as plain text output for scripts. It can export the analysis to JSON, import a saved JSON file, or store results in SQLite or BadgerDB for later reuse. Scans can be filtered by ignored paths (plain or regex patterns, .gitignore-style files), file types, mtime ranges, and filesystem boundaries. Interactive use supports deletion (which can be disabled with --no-delete), viewing files, and spawning a shell. The README also describes a web UI with a treemap and donut chart, plus a "cleanup projections" view that highlights regenerable caches and build directories without deleting anything.
use_cases: find what is filling up my disk
analyze disk usage on a Linux server over SSH
export disk usage report to JSON
find the largest files in a directory
compare directory sizes in a browser treemap
identify safe-to-delete caches and build folders
notable: Web UI with treemap, donut chart, and cleanup projections embedded in the binary
Memory-efficient non-interactive mode that tracks only top-level totals
Can browse inside tar and zip archives with --archive-browsing
Optional SQLite or BadgerDB storage to reload past analyses without rescanning
Benchmarks against ncdu, dua, dust, du, and others in the README
caveats: README says it is aimed primarily at SSDs; HDDs work but gain less from parallelism
Web UI deletion and reveal rely on a per-run token and loopback origin checks; binding to a non-loopback address exposes scan details on the network
Deleting while a filter is active is blocked unless GDU_ALLOW_DELETE_WITH_FILTER=1 is set
keywords: what is using my disk space
